proposals.whyText:
# Why: notes-json-flag
Added a `--json` store_true flag to the `list` subparser and a branch in `cmd_list` that dumps the notes list as JSON when set. The default path (the "no notes yet" message and the `#id: text` lines) is untouched, so human-readable output is unchanged. With no notes, `--json` emits `[]`, which keeps the output valid JSON. I did not alter the storage format, the other commands, or the argument parsing structure beyond the one new flag.

proposals.whyText:
# Why: notes-search
Added a `search` subcommand that takes a query and prints notes whose text contains it, compared case-insensitively by lowercasing both sides. It reuses the existing `load()` helper and prints "no matches" when nothing matches, as the acceptance criteria require. Matching output uses the same `#id: text` format as `list`. Nothing else was changed: `add`, `list`, `delete`, storage, and the argument parser's other subcommands are untouched.

proposals.whyText:
# Why: notes-due-date
Added an optional `--due DATE` argument to the `add` subparser, defaulting to None. In `cmd_add`, the `due` key is written onto the note object only when the flag is provided, so notes added without `--due` keep their original shape. The date is stored as a raw string without validation, since the spec only asks for storage and format validation was not requested. `list` and `delete` were deliberately left unchanged, as the spec scopes the work to `add`.
